title: Day of the Week Effect in biotechnology stocks: An Application of the GARCH processes

extraction.methodology_summary: The paper investigates the day-of-the-week effect in the NASDAQ Biotechnology Index (NBI) using daily returns from January 2002 to December 2015. It incorporates Fama-French risk factors, the Carhart momentum factor, and utilizes GARCH, EGARCH, and GJR-GARCH processes to model volatility and test the significance of return differences across weekdays, comparing pre-ACA and post-ACA subperiods.
extraction.universe: NASDAQ Biotechnology Index (NBI) consisting of 117 listed companies.
key_findings: Biotechnology stock returns were lowest on Mondays and significantly higher on Wednesdays, Thursdays, and Fridays over the 2002-2015 period.
The day-of-the-week effect in biotechnology stocks persisted even after controlling for Fama-French risk factors and Carhart momentum.
The day-of-the-week effect disappeared in the period following the passage of the Affordable Care Act (ACA) on March 30, 2010.
Momentum (UMD) and the small-firm effect (SMB) were positively associated with market risk-adjusted biotechnology returns across the GARCH models.
limitations: The post-ACA period may not be long enough to fully estimate the day-of-the-week effect.
Possible confounding from macroeconomic changes as the economy recovered from the 2008 great recession.
extraction.extraction_notes: No standard strategy backtest performance metrics (such as Sharpe ratio or annualized strategy return) are reported in the paper; the quantitative results focus entirely on regression coefficients and descriptive statistics, so performance_metrics is empty.
